what_it_does: AI accelerators need to talk to each other at high speeds when training huge models on multiple chips. This paper describes a specialized small chip (called a chiplet) that converts data between electrical signals (how chips normally communicate) and optical signals (light pulses, which move much faster over long distances). It follows the UCIe standard, which is an industry rule for how chips should connect. The chiplet sits at the boundary between the electrical and optical worlds, letting multiple AI accelerator chips work together as one faster system.
